sentences.text: Heard on I.A.No.22829/2024, an application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail on behalf of the appellant - Anil Kumar.

This criminal appeal assails the judgment dated 02-03-2024 passed in S.T.No.10/2021 by the Additional Judge to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Lahar District Bhind whereby the appellant has been convicted as under:
Section Imprisonment Fine 420 of IPC 7 years' RI Rs.10,000/- with  default stipulation.

It is the submission of learned counsel for appellant that the trial Court erred in convicting and awarding jail sentence to the appellant -Anil Kumar.
Appellant is a Government servant and is Post Master in India Post and suffered confinement for more than 8 months as pre and post trial detention.
It is further submitted that earlier vide order dated 22-03-2024 an application for suspension of sentence of appellant was rejected on merits.
However, thereafter appellant and complainant entered into an agreement and they settled the matter once and for all.
For that an application under Section 320 of Cr.P.C. along with affidavits of respective parties were filed.

One of the co-accused (similarly placed Post Master) also preferred petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
wherein the said accused and complainant entered into compromise and charge-sheet against him has already been quashed vide order dated 06-08-2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.32207/2024.

Even otherwise role of the appellant is confined to accepting money IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH AT GWALIOR CRA NO. 3250 OF 2024 (ANIL KUMAR VS. STATE OF M.P.) which has been given by a Government recognized agent to deposit in Post Office.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH AT GWALIOR CRA NO. 3250 OF 2024 (ANIL KUMAR VS. STATE OF M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He was not in direct touch with the original complainant who tried to deposit the amount in Post Office through a recognized agent.
Due to mischief intermediary/recognized collection agent, appellant is suffering confinement and his sufferings are writ large including adversity in service.

Learned counsel for the appellant also referred judgment of Apex Court in the case of Ramgopal & Another Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2021(4) JLJ 1 and referred para 11 and 13 to bring home the analogy that criminal proceedings involving non-heinous offences or where the offences are pre-dominantly of a private nature, can be annulled irrespective of the fact that trial has already been concluded or appeal stands dismissed against conviction.

entities.text: Ramgopal & Another Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2021(4) JLJ 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Here, appeal is still pending, therefore, benefit of suspension of sentence be given.
Appellant has good case on merits and hearing of appeal would take some time.
Thus, prayed for grant of suspension of sentence.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the application and prayed for its dismissal.

Learned counsel for the complainant Shri Bhadoriya categorically submits that matter has been settled between him and appellant and he has no objection if suspension of sentence is granted in favour of appellant.

sentences.text: Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, this Court intends to allow the application for suspension of sentence (I.A.No.22829/2024).

If appellant furnishes bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) along with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court that he shall appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court on 20-12-2024 and on all other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Office for appearance, then he shall be released on bail and execution of jail sentence is Anil Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189608184/
2 suspended till disposal of this appeal, subject to deposit of fine amount.
At this stage, learned counsel for the appellant expressed his willingness to advance arguments finally as matter pertains to service prospects of an employee who never had any criminal record earlier.

entities.text: Anil Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh

sentences.text: Respondent has no objection to this proposition.

As prayed, list this case in the month of December,
2024 for final hearing at motion stage.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for information and necessary compliance.
